A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ERM research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and appendix expansion.

before.justification: v1 reports original seven-dataset benchmark results, component ablations, optimization-step comparisons, and an appendix exemplar-retrieval experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and additionally reports token consumption and component execution times in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Exemplar-Guided Reflection, Feedback Memory, and Exemplar Factory retain their procedures, filtering, priority updates, and five-exemplar retrieval. Symbol clarifications and the meta-prompt placeholder rename do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate LIAR, BBH-navigate, ETHOS, ArSarcasm, WebNLG, GSM8K, and WSC. Added efficiency measurements and cases concern existing tasks. Multimodal tasks appear only in expanded related work.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparator sets and exemplar-retrieval controls are retained. APO is renamed consistently to ProTeGi, referring to the same work. New Table 9 measures token consumption for already evaluated APE, OPRO, GPO, and ProTeGi.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds total-token evaluation on LIAR and average timing breakdowns for optimization and inference. Existing dataset splits, task metrics, model versions, temperatures, eight-candidate optimization setting, and few-shot protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds focused computational-cost analyses and feedback-combination cases for LIAR, BBH, and GSM8K in Tables 12–14. These add preceding prompts and sampled feedback; the BBH and GSM8K optimized passages already appeared in v1 Figures 12 and 24. Existing ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are repeated three times and report averages. v2 adds no seeds, dispersion estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests; its timing averages do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Scores in Tables 1–6 and the exemplar comparison, renumbered from Table 9 to Table 10, are unchanged. New Table 9 reports 7,503 tokens for ERM versus 12,836 for ProTeGi. Table 11 adds optimization API/memory times of 28.161/0.062 seconds and inference API/retrieval times of 1.201/0.029 seconds.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 retain the same objective, sampling rules, priority update, and forgetting criterion. Sample-count symbols, score notation, and set notation are clarified without changing the underlying mathematics. No new assumptions, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the three-component contribution, seven-task evaluation, 10.1-point LIAR F1 advantage, and approximately halved optimization-step claim. Additional cost evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix D discusses correcting exemplar labels, adding reasoning or human feedback, and distinguishes indirect improvements through feedback from direct exemplar benefits. Appendix C interprets token and timing costs. The original limitations concerning persistent errors, human intervention, and restricted task coverage remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies an A800 GPU for BGE-M3 in the timing analysis and reports component execution times. Existing model identifiers, temperatures, candidate counts, dataset access information, and prompt templates remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds discussion and citations covering multi-step and multimodal optimization, including PROMST, VisLingInstruct, and OPT2I; the introduction also adds Evoke. ERM's central positioning remains unchanged. Publication updates for existing references are not new cited works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized introduction and method rewrites, clarifies notation, and revises author information. Appendix C becomes More Experiments, a More Discussion section is inserted, and the former appendices D/E become E/F. Most existing prose and prompt content is retained.

P2.justification: The document is broadly retypeset, including changed typography and conversion of appendix prose from single to double columns. Five tables are added, including colored feedback-to-prompt case displays; existing tables and prompt figures are reflowed. Figures 1–3 retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: v1 supports efficiency mainly through optimization-step counts; v2 adds token consumption and component timings, strengthening that evidence. Feedback traces and hardware disclosure also improve transparency. These gains are limited: benchmark results and ablations are unchanged, case outputs are partly reused, and proposed human intervention remains unevaluated.
